$schema_note: Flag registry for Empire Builder. Each entry pairs with a PNG in assets/flags/ (see docs/02-capital-and-flags.md and assets/flags/README.md). The game lists any flag that has BOTH a PNG on disk AND an entry here. These 6 entries are the user-supplied flags (5 historical designs + 1 royal variant), recreated as faithful vector art and rasterized to PNG; drop in your own PNG with the same filename to override any of them. Balance rule: total power budget <= ~10 per flag (1% ~= 1 pt, a 'special' ~= 3-5 pts).

flags.name: The Imperial Eagle
flags.symbolism: A crowned double-headed eagle on cloth-of-gold, one head watching East and one West, gripping a sword (temporal power) and a globus cruciger — the cross-bearing orb of sovereignty over the whole world. It proclaims a realm that rules two worlds at once and never sleeps.
flags.flavor: Flown above a capital that claims to be the center of the world. The twin heads mean no border is ever left unwatched, and no throne is ever left unguarded.

flags.name: The Labarum
flags.symbolism: The sacred monogram (the Chi-Rho) in gold on a field of imperial red, carried at the head of the army. It is the sign of divine favor in war: 'by this sign, conquer.'
flags.flavor: The standard that turned a warlord into an emperor. Soldiers who march behind the monogram believe the heavens march with them, and they do not break easily.

flags.name: The Holy Cross
flags.symbolism: A pure white cross with flared arms on a field of blood-red: martial faith and a sworn order. The red is the sacrifice of those who hold the wall; the white cross is the vow they hold it for.
flags.flavor: The banner of a holy order sworn to defend the realm's frontier. Where the White Cross flies over a wall, the line has never yet fallen.

flags.name: The Sun of Vergina
flags.symbolism: The radiant sixteen-rayed star of a conquering dynasty, blazing gold on red. It is the sun of a golden age and the emblem of a people whose ambition marched to the edge of the world.
flags.flavor: Emblazoned on the shields of the phalanx that never lost a pitched battle. A sun that, they swore, would set on no empire of theirs.

flags.name: The Eternal Ankh
flags.symbolism: The golden key of life on a deep river-red field: vitality, fertility, and the unbroken cycle of a people who never diminish. It is a promise that the land will never empty.
flags.flavor: Raised over a civilization that measures its wealth in living souls. Under the Ankh, families flourish and the cradles are never quiet.

flags.name: The Descending Dove
flags.symbolism: A golden dove stooping from on high upon a field of imperial purple — grace and the spirit descending, a mandate granted from above rather than seized from below.
flags.flavor: Said to have alighted on the founder's standard at the first dawn. A people who rule because heaven, not the sword, chose them.

flags.name: The Crimson Eagle
flags.symbolism: A blood-red eagle displayed on cloth-of-gold, wings spread and talons bared — martial vigilance and a warrior aristocracy that watches every horizon.
flags.flavor: Carried by the mountain lords who counted their worth in spears. The eagle does not ask leave to hunt.

flags.name: The Elder Rune
flags.symbolism: A single gold rune on purple — the graven word of the ancestors, fate and hard-won wisdom carved into stone that outlasts kings.
flags.flavor: No one living recalls who first cut the sign, only that oaths sworn beneath it have never been safely broken.

flags.name: The Ringed Cross
flags.symbolism: A cross of gold ringed in gold, with four bezants for the four corners of the world, on a field of red — one faith binding the whole earth in order and coin.
flags.flavor: Struck on the first coins of the realm as much as sewn on its banners. Devotion and treasury, minted together.

flags.name: The Imperial Eagle (Porphyrogennetos)
flags.symbolism: The same gold field and black eagle, now framed in a double border of Tyrian purple — 'born in the purple', the mature, sovereign form of the founding banner, unfurled only when a settlement of soldiers becomes a seat of emperors.
flags.flavor: Purple was the color no commoner could wear. To ring the golden eagle in it is to declare the realm has passed from ambition into legend.

flags.name: The Golden Rho
flags.symbolism: A single golden rho on a white field — rule (basileia) distilled to one letter. The quiet confidence of a house that needs no beasts or blades on its banner.
flags.flavor: Raised by the scholar-kings who rebuilt an empire from exile; where the Rho flies, the archives are full and the tax rolls are honest.
